generated.answer: Ranged attack style has the largest range of possible attack ranges among weapon types. Ranged weapons vary from as low as 1 tile (salamanders, no longrange option) up to 10 tiles (long-range crossbows on longrange), giving the greatest spread of possible attack ranges (3–10 tiles for normal attacks, with longrange extending some up to 10). In contrast, melee weapons are almost uniformly 1 tile (with halberds at 2, and a few special attacks reaching up to 3 or even 11 tiles), and Magic spells are mostly fixed at 10 tiles for combat spells, with powered staves varying only between 6 and 8 (10 with longrange). Thus, the Ranged attack style shows the widest variety/range of possible attack distances across its weapons.

question.question: In the combat triangle, which attack styles are strong against which?
question.gold_answer: Warriors are strong against rangers. Rangers are strong against mages. Mages are strong against warriors.

generated.query: In the combat triangle, which attack styles are strong against which?
generated.answer:
The OSRS combat triangle works as follows: Melee (Warriors) is strong against Ranged (Rangers), Ranged (Rangers) is strong against Magic (Mages), and Magic (Mages) is strong against Melee (Warriors).

- Melee vs Ranged: Warriors' armour deflects arrows/projectiles, and their weapons penetrate the leather armour worn by rangers, making melee effective against ranged users.
- Ranged vs Magic: Rangers' leather/dragonhide armour absorbs spells, and their projectiles pierce through a mage's robes easily, letting rangers take down mages quickly due to mages' weak defensive armour.
- Magic vs Melee: Mages' spells are amplified by the metallic armour typically worn by warriors and can hit through melee armour fairly easily, especially if mages keep their distance, making magic strong against melee.

It's important to note that the triangle is only a general rule of thumb - it does not strictly determine the outcome of any fight, as any combat style can be used effectively against any other.

citations.claim: Melee tends to be effective against rangers, ranged tends to be effective against mages, and magic tends to be strong against warriors.

chunk.text:
Old School RuneScape follows the combat triangle , a design philosophy dictating that melee tends to be effective against rangers , ranged tends to be effective against mages , and magic tends to be strong against warriors. This philosophy manifests in the combat bonuses of armour and weapons, the ability of ranged and magic to attack from a distance or safespot , and weapon/armour/spell effects (such as the twisted bow 's increased damage against monsters with high magic level).

In terms of bonuses, melee armour tends to excel in melee defence and ranged defence; ranged armour tends to have substantial ranged attack, high magic defence, and middling melee and ranged defences; and magic armour tends to offer magic attack bonuses and middling magic defence, but little to no ranged or melee defence.

In general, when players are combating opponents with similar combat skill, the combat triangle can offer a rule of thumb as to which combat style is most effective. It should be noted that the combat triangle in no-way defines a fight outcome; any combat style can be used effectively to kill opponents using any other combat style, the triangle simply suggests what is favourable.

The three combat styles have a colour coding which many game elements follow: Melee is conveyed by red, Ranged by green, and Magic by blue. Examples include Scurrius 's and The Hueycoatl 's long-distance attacks, so that the player knows which protection prayer to use, as well as the Sigils in the Chasm of Fire .

Monkey Guards are level 167 gorillas that reside in the Temple of Marimbo , found on Ape Atoll . They reside on the ground floor [ UK ] 1 st floor [ US ] and 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of Ape Atoll 's Temple of Marimbo and are the strongest guard found on Ape Atoll. They have a large amount of health and throw vicious punches that can hit up to 14. When they have very low health, they will beat their chest, causing them to heal 25 hitpoints , which is about 20% of their maximum health; they appear to be able to do this indefinitely but only while in melee range. Monkey Guards drop larger versions of monkey bones, which give 18 prayer experience points when buried. However, these are not tradeable.

Bearded monkey guards can be a nuisance because they cannot be walked through. After exiting the Temple of Marimbo Dungeon , bearded Monkey Guards can block the player from exiting the temple. Either wait or climb up the ladder near the trapdoor.

There is a way, however, to kill the Monkey Guards (including bearded variants) using melee as a player with relatively low combat stats. Monkey Guards can be brought down to 26-35 HP by normal attacks. The player can then poison the Monkey Guard using a Dragon dagger(p++) or other super-poisoned weapon. Once the Monkey Guard is poisoned, and before the Monkey Guard heals, the player can run out of range of the poisoned Monkey Guard, and wait for the poison damage to finish him off. The south-western corner of the Monkey Guard temple is a good place to poison and safespot one of the Monkey Guards, as there is a ladder that the player can hide behind. They still use their healing ability when being flinched , however. Alternatively, you can safespot them and use ranged to easily kill them as they won't use their healing ability when they can't attack you.

It is possible to utilise the stairs near the prayer altar to bypass the healing, though this technique is precise and tedious. Further, the monkey guard may not cooperate by wandering away while you are on the second floor. Best done with a 4 tick weapon.

question.question: When does a ring of life teleport you?
question.gold_answer: When your hitpoints dip below 10% of their maximum value.

generated.query: When does a ring of life teleport you?
generated.answer:
A ring of life triggers when the wearer is attacked and drops to 10% or less of their maximum Hitpoints (as long as that hit doesn't kill them outright), automatically teleporting the wearer to their respawn point (or East Ardougne if toggled after completing the medium Ardougne Diary). The ring crumbles to dust after this single use. Note that it does not guarantee safety if a hit brings you from above 10% straight to 0, and it won't cure poison. Self-inflicted damage sources like a dwarven rock cake or locator orb can also trigger it, and if worn with a phoenix necklace, the necklace's effect triggers first. In Wintertodt, it activates instead when your warmth drops below 10%. In PvP, the Tele Block spell prevents the ring's teleport from activating, though its teleport otherwise works up to level 30 Wilderness (unlike most other teleports, which stop working above level 20 Wilderness).</answer>

Summer pie is a type of pie with two bites that restores 11 Hitpoints , 10% run energy , and grants a +5 temporary skill boost to Agility per bite. A pie dish will remain after consumption.

It can be created by baking a raw summer pie on a cooking range , requiring level 95 Cooking and granting 260 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Summer pies never stop burning altogether even at level 99, unless the player is wearing a Cooking cape . Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.

Summer pies are a type of 1 tick (0.6 seconds) fast food , meaning you can eat them in succession with less delay than standard food which adds a 3-tick (1.8 second) penalty. Because of this short eat delay, summer pies can restore health quicker than manta rays , making them more efficient for healing up a lot of lost health in the same amount of ticks. However, as each half adds 3 ticks of attack delay, they are less efficient in combat than other high-healing foods.

The +5 Agility boost makes summer pies a great food for use in Agility training, increasing the chance to pass obstacles while restoring Hitpoints lost from failing any. It may also be used to pass Agility level requirements in quests , Agility courses , shortcuts or any other activities with an Agility requirement . Not all requirements can be boosted, such as Dragon Slayer II , the Ape Atoll Agility Course or Saradomin's Encampment in the God Wars Dungeon . The Preserve prayer may be used to extend the duration of the boost.

Summer pies are popular for fighting the Chaos Elemental or Chaos Fanatic as the empty pie dish prevents their special attacks from un-equipping Worn Equipment due to a full inventory.

Successfully baking a summer pie inside of the Cooks' Guild is an elite Varrock Diary task.

chunk.text:
Old School RuneScape follows the combat triangle , a design philosophy dictating that melee tends to be effective against rangers , ranged tends to be effective against mages , and magic tends to be strong against warriors. This philosophy manifests in the combat bonuses of armour and weapons, the ability of ranged and magic to attack from a distance or safespot , and weapon/armour/spell effects (such as the twisted bow 's increased damage against monsters with high magic level).

In terms of bonuses, melee armour tends to excel in melee defence and ranged defence; ranged armour tends to have substantial ranged attack, high magic defence, and middling melee and ranged defences; and magic armour tends to offer magic attack bonuses and middling magic defence, but little to no ranged or melee defence.

In general, when players are combating opponents with similar combat skill, the combat triangle can offer a rule of thumb as to which combat style is most effective. It should be noted that the combat triangle in no-way defines a fight outcome; any combat style can be used effectively to kill opponents using any other combat style, the triangle simply suggests what is favourable.

The three combat styles have a colour coding which many game elements follow: Melee is conveyed by red, Ranged by green, and Magic by blue. Examples include Scurrius 's and The Hueycoatl 's long-distance attacks, so that the player knows which protection prayer to use, as well as the Sigils in the Chasm of Fire .

chunk.text: Mages are strong against warriors as long as they keep their distance. Their magic is amplified by the metallic armours usually worn by warriors. Mage-based armour (robes) offers little protection against any of the three combat styles. Spells can hit through melee armour fairly easily. They can also freeze , bind , weaken , confuse , or stun their opponents, giving magic the highest utility of the combat styles. For players to be effective mages, freezing melee combatants is essential. Magic is rarely used alone and is most effective when combined with another combat style - usually ranged, combining the utility of a mage with the distanced damage of a ranger. Magic suffers from a far lower maximum hit than other combat styles - Ice Barrage is tied with the god spells with a maximum base damage of only 30, potentially boostable to 48 with the maximum damage-boosting items and Flames of Zamorak . Ranged and melee can hit over twice as hard as this with special attacks from weapons such as the Dark Bow and Dragon Claws. Added to this, magic is most often out-performed in damage per second by a similarly levelled and geared user of another style, however this does not mean magic cannot deal considerable damage with higher level spells.

chunk.section_path: Using Slayer reward points > Cancelling and blocking tasks
chunk.text:
Slayer reward points are mainly used to cancel undesirable tasks, which offer slow experience, poor profit or mediocre experience but take too long to complete. Cancelling a task costs 30 reward points each time, making it potentially expensive to try and get a specific assignment.

Tasks that the player does not wish to ever do can be permanently blocked. The cost to block a task differs depending on the Slayer master:

Turael / Aya and Spria : 40 points Mazchna / Achtryn : 50 points Vannaka : 60 points Chaeldar : 70 points Konar quo Maten : 80 points Nieve / Steve : 90 points Duradel / Kuradal : 100 points Krystilia : 100 points Mortimer : 120 points

Each Slayer master has their own individual block list. Up to seven assigned monsters (or monster groups) can be blocked per Slayer master, except for Mortimer, who only has two block slots. To block an assignment, 50 quest points are required per slot, totaling up to 300 quest points for six slots. A seventh slot is available only with the completion of the elite Lumbridge & Draynor Diary . For toggled tasks like lizardmen, the player should simply cancel the toggle and the task itself, so that they cannot obtain the task anymore, which essentially acts as a block. With 500 Slayer points, a block can be applied to Fossil Island Wyverns. While significantly more expensive than any task block in-game, the player has the ability to freely toggle on and off this block as they desire.

The main goal for Slayer training is to spend as much time as possible doing good tasks, and as little time as possible doing bad tasks. As such, it is best to make use of all the available blocks as soon as possible, and then use the cancel option as often as it can be used while maintaining a stable level of Slayer reward points. Players are also strongly advised to keep enough points in reserve to cancel several tasks in a row, in case of multiple undesirable assignments being given.

Kruk plays a minor role in Monkey Madness I . The player must speak to him to be escorted to King Awowogei and continue the quest.

In Monkey Madness II , the player, after successfully navigating through Kruk's Dungeon , defeats him and takes his paw to make a Kruk greegree . It is then revealed that Kruk has been secretly helping Glough with his experiments , capturing monkeys for him to use as specimens. When the player, impersonating Kruk, informs Awowogei of the failed plans that they sabotaged, he strips Kruk of his ranks and duties and later replaces him with Duke .

''In which our hero/heroine finds himself/herself contending with life as a monkey.''

In this chapter, you will be required to speak with King Awowogei and retrieve a monkey from the Ardougne Zoo . After the conversation ends, he will conveniently take you back to King Awowogei .

3- Speak to Awowogei and offer an alliance, and he will ask you to rescue a monkey from the Ardougne Zoo . Teleport out and make your way to Ardougne.

One dose of anti-venom will completely cure venom and provide immunity for 36-54 seconds. Anti-venom+ provides immunity to venom for three minutes. Extended anti-venom+ provides immunity for approximately 6.3 minutes.

Eating a strange fruit will completely cure venom and provide immunity for about 18 seconds, but cannot be used to mitigate special attacks from a Dreadborn Araxyte .

Drinking a Guthix rest or Sanfew serum , the secondary heal after eating cooked moonlight antelope , casting the Cure Me on the Lunar Spellbook , and using the prayer book from The Great Brain Robbery quest while wearing a holy symbol or hallowed symbol , are all additional options to reduce venom to poison.

The Ornate rejuvenation pool , Elidinis Statuette and Pool of Refreshment will also cure venom. Leaving a Player-owned house also cures venom.

The Serpentine helm , while worn, provides full immunity to being envenomed and poisoned.

The Noxious halberd special attack completely cures venom, at the cost of 50% special attack energy. This special attack also has the added benefit of increasing the player's next successful hit to a minimum based on the venom hitsplat.

A m'speak amulet is an item crafted during Monkey Madness I that allows the player to communicate with monkeys . It is later used in the Recipe for Disaster Awowogei subquest as well as Monkey Madness II . After completion of Monkey Madness II, the amulet is no longer needed to speak with monkeys (though the amulet is no longer used after Chapter III of the quest).

To make one, the player must take monkey dentures , a m'amulet mould , and a gold bar to Zooknock , who will give them an enchanted bar (and the mould back). They must then use the bar on the wall of flame in the Temple of Marimbo Dungeon with the mould in their inventory to create an unstrung m'speak amulet . The amulet can be completed using a ball of wool or the String Jewellery spell.

If the m'speak amulet is lost, it can be reobtained by repeating the above steps, or if Monkey Madness II has been completed, by speaking with Zooknock in the Tree Gnome Stronghold .

Since Zooknock returns the m'amulet mould to the player when the bar is created, only one mould is required to create two or more enchanted bars.
